commitResults.messageTitle: Add persistent task storage for Level 7

commitResults.messageBody:
Store Deadline's `by` field as LocalDate instead of a raw String so
invalid dates are caught at input time and displayed consistently
(MMM dd uuuu) instead of echoing back whatever text the user typed.

- TBlade parses /by as yyyy-MM-dd and reports a corrective error
  message if the format is wrong.
- Storage.parseTask is wrapped in try/catch so a corrupted or
  unparseable saved line is skipped instead of crashing on load.
- ui-test-plan.md updated to use yyyy-MM-dd inputs and reflect the
  new MMM dd uuuu display format.

Extract Ui, Parser, and TaskList out of TBlade to make the design
more OOP, following the class breakdown suggested by the increment
(Storage already existed from Level-7).

- Ui owns all console I/O: banner/greeting, reading commands, and
  every printed confirmation/error/listing.
- Parser owns turning raw command text into validated arguments
  (todo description, deadline /by, event /from and /to, task
  index), returning DeadlineArgs/EventArgs records instead of
  TBlade doing inline substring parsing.
- TaskList wraps the task List and now owns the 100-task capacity
  check as its own invariant, rather than an external helper.
- Storage takes its file path via constructor (new Storage(filePath))
  instead of a hardcoded path constant, matching the increment's
  sample Duke(String filePath) signature.

TBlade is now a thin coordinator: it wires these four together and
keeps only command dispatch (equals/startsWith routing, including
the bye/list "no extra text" checks) in its run loop. Behavior is
unchanged - verified against the full ui-test-plan.md suite.

Organize the flat src/main/java/*.java classes into packages under
tblade, grouped by responsibility (stretch goal: multiple packages,
since a single package would already be crowded at 11 classes):

- tblade            TBlade (entry point / coordinator)
- tblade.task       Task, TaskType, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList
- tblade.parser     Parser
- tblade.ui         Ui
- tblade.storage    Storage
- tblade.exception  TBladeException

src/main/java remains the source root, as required. Update the
test-ui runner script to compile sources recursively (**/*.java)
and invoke the new tblade.TBlade main class, and fix a stale
src/main/java/TBlade.java path in README.md. Behavior unchanged -
verified against the full ui-test-plan.md suite.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge add-gradle-support and point build at TBlade
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring in the template's Gradle scaffolding for A-Gradle (build.gradle,
gradle wrapper, gradlew scripts) from add-gradle-support per the
increment's Step 1, then update build.gradle's placeholder
seedu.duke.Duke references to this project's actual entry point:

- application.mainClass: seedu.duke.Duke -> tblade.TBlade
- shadowJar.archiveFileName: duke.jar -> tblade.jar

Verified: ./gradlew build succeeds, ./gradlew run behaves identically
to the manual javac build, and the ui-test-plan.md suite still passes.

Add a JUnit 5 test suite (40 tests) under src/test/java, mirroring
the main package structure, going toward the stretch goal (all
non-trivial classes, not just the minimal two):

- TodoTest / DeadlineTest / EventTest / TaskListTest: task creation,
  mark/unmark, toString formatting (incl. Deadline's MMM dd uuuu
  display), and TaskList's 100-task capacity limit.
- ParserTest: every validation branch for todo/deadline/event/
  task-index parsing - the most branch-heavy class in the app.
- StorageTest: save/load round trip across all task types and done
  status, a missing-file case, and tolerance of corrupted lines.
- UiTest: printed console output, verified via System.out capture.

TBlade's run loop is left untested here (it's a console read-eval
loop, integration-level rather than a unit), as is
TBladeException's one-line pass-through constructor.

Verify the app packages into a standalone executable JAR via the
existing shadowJar task (configured in A-Gradle) and document how
to run it.

Built build/libs/tblade.jar and confirmed it runs correctly with
no classpath, exactly as required: copied into an empty folder and
launched with `java -jar "tblade.jar"`, then re-run in the same
folder to confirm saved tasks reload from the data folder created
next to the jar. No build.gradle changes were needed - Main-Class
and the output jar name were already set correctly.

Add a "Running the JAR file" section to README.md pointing users
at the releases page and the java -jar command.

Close the remaining Javadoc gaps to reach the stretch goal (header
comments on all non-private classes/methods, plus non-trivial
private methods) rather than just the minimal half-coverage bar.
Most of the codebase was already documented throughout prior
increments per AGENTS.md; this fills in what was missed:

- Todo/Deadline/Event.getTimeDetails(): these @Override methods had
  no doc comment of their own.
- TaskType's enum constants (TODO/DEADLINE/EVENT): flagged by the
  javadoc tool as undocumented public fields.
- Parser.DeadlineArgs/EventArgs: added @param docs for each record
  component; documented the private no-arg constructor's purpose.

Verified: `javadoc` now generates with zero warnings; ./gradlew
test (40 tests) and the ui-test-plan.md suite both still pass.

Add the seedu-java-coding-standard and seedu-git-standard project
skills, based on the SE-EDU intermediate Java and git conventions
guides, and mandate both in AGENTS.md for all future code and
commits in this project. Add present-changes-visually, a skill for
rendering a diff as a published Artifact for visual review.

Audit the existing codebase against the Java standard: naming,
brace style, import order, and Javadoc format were already
compliant from prior increments. The only violations were two
error messages in TBlade.java over the 120-char hard limit; wrap
both.

Verified: ./gradlew test (40 tests) and the ui-test-plan.md suite
both still pass.

Give users a way to find tasks by keyword.

- TaskList.find(keyword): returns matching tasks (description
  contains keyword), preserving order.
- Parser.getFindKeyword: extracts/validates the find command's
  keyword, same shape as getTodoDescription.
- Ui.showMatchingTasks: separate message from showTaskList, since
  the header text differs ("matching tasks" vs "tasks").
- TBlade: wire up find/find <keyword> dispatch; add find to both
  command-list error messages, wrapping them under the 120-char
  line limit per the project's Java coding standard.

Add JUnit coverage for the keyword extraction and search logic,
and a ui-test-plan.md case reproducing the level's example output
exactly. Verified: ./gradlew test (45 tests) and the full
ui-test-plan.md suite (8 cases) both pass.

Resolve a conflict in TBlade.java: both branch-A-CodingStandard and
branch-Level-9 rewrote the same two command-list error messages
(wrapping them under the 120-char line limit). Keep branch-Level-9's
version in both spots - it is a strict superset, carrying the same
line-wrap plus "find" added to the command list.

Verified post-merge: ./gradlew test (45 tests), the full
ui-test-plan.md suite (8 cases), and a line-length sweep (0
violations) all pass.

Add Checkstyle, enforcing the mechanically-checkable subset of the
project's Java coding standard automatically, as a backstop to the
seedu-java-coding-standard skill (which still covers judgment calls
Checkstyle can't, like whether a name or Javadoc summary is good).

- Copy config/checkstyle/{checkstyle.xml,suppressions.xml} from
  AddressBook-Level3, the SE-EDU reference config for this exact
  standard.
- Add the checkstyle Gradle plugin; ./gradlew check and build now
  run it automatically alongside the tests.
- Add a pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit) that blocks a commit
  on violations; activate it locally via core.hooksPath and
  document the one-time per-clone setup in README.md.

Fix the two real violations Checkstyle found that the manual audit
had missed: switch/case indentation in Storage.java (case must be
indented in from switch, not flush with it), and lambda line-wrap
placement in 12 ParserTest.java assertThrows calls (an opening `(`
must stay attached to the previous line). Document the case-indent
rule in the coding-standard skill so future edits match without a
follow-up fix.

Verified: ./gradlew build (checkstyle + 45 tests + jar) and the
full ui-test-plan.md suite both pass; the hook was manually tested
blocking and then passing.

Add a JavaFX GUI, following the tutorial's final (Part 4, FXML)
architecture directly rather than its intermediate non-FXML steps,
per the tutorial's own suggestion once you're happy with the design.
The console UI is kept working too, per the assignment's recommendation
(easier to test).

- build.gradle: JavaFX dependency block copied verbatim from the
  tutorial (17.0.7, win/mac/linux classifiers) rather than an
  AI-improvised alternative, to avoid a Frankenstein cross-platform
  build. application.mainClass now points at the GUI's Launcher.
- tblade.gui.{Launcher,Main,MainWindow,DialogBox}: the tutorial's
  FXML-based structure, adapted to this project's package and
  TBlade. MainWindow closes the window ~1s after a "bye" response,
  so the goodbye message is visible first.
- Ui/TBlade refactor: split each response into a pure formatX()
  method (no I/O) plus one generic showMessage() for CLI printing.
  This lets TBlade.getResponse(String), the GUI's entry point, reuse
  the exact same wording as the console UI instead of duplicating
  it. CLI output is unchanged - verified byte-identical against the
  full ui-test-plan.md suite.
- Fix a real bug caught during manual testing: the ScrollPane only
  scrolled horizontally, never vertically. The tutorial's FXML
  snippet for Part 4 omits fitToWidth="true", even though its own
  earlier non-FXML code sets it; without it, dialog labels never
  get a width to wrap against. Added it back.
- Generated placeholder avatars (a silhouette, and a pig face
  matching the CLI's own 🐷 branding) since the tutorial's originals
  aren't available to reuse.
- Corrected the seedu-java-coding-standard skill's import-order
  section: Checkstyle's CustomImportOrder buckets javafx.* and this
  project's own tblade.* into the same catch-all group, not
  separate ones as previously documented.

Verified: ./gradlew build (checkstyle + 45 tests + jar), the full
ui-test-plan.md suite, and manual GUI testing (including the
scroll-direction bug, fixed above) all pass.

Add TaskList.of(Task... tasks), a varargs factory for building a
small fixed task list in one line (mirrors List.of(...)).

This is the one genuine fit in the codebase: 12 places in the test
suite built a TaskList via new TaskList() + several .add() calls,
which is verbose and forces "throws TBladeException" onto the test
method since add() enforces the capacity check. Convert those call
sites to TaskList.of(...) and drop the now-unneeded throws clauses;
add a test for of() itself.

Left add_atCapacity_throwsTBladeException (loops to 100 tasks) and
add_belowCapacity_appendsTask (tests add() itself) as they were -
neither fits a varargs conversion. No production code needed this:
TBlade/Storage always build task lists from a dynamically-sized
source (a loaded file), never a small fixed set of literals.

Verified: ./gradlew build (checkstyle + 46 tests + jar) and the
full ui-test-plan.md suite both pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use assertions to document internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Several places in the code rely on assumptions that are never
violated in practice but were previously undocumented and
unenforced — a future change could silently break them without any
signal until a confusing downstream failure.

Add java assert statements (not JUnit assertions) at three such
points, each paired with a message explaining why the assumption
holds:
- TaskList.get()/remove(): the index is always in range, because
  every caller validates it against size() via
  Parser.parseTaskIndex() first.
- Storage.formatTask(): a task's TaskType always matches its
  concrete class, because each Task subclass's constructor is the
  only place that pairs them.
- MainWindow.handleUserInput(): tblade is never null when input can
  occur, because Main.start() injects it before showing the stage.

Verified each fires under -ea (which Gradle's test task enables by
default) without breaking any existing test, and is a no-op when
assertions are disabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic numbers in Parser with named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser extracted command arguments using hardcoded numeric literals
(substring(4), substring(8), byIndex + 4, fromIndex + 6, etc.) that
were really the lengths of the command words and delimiters (todo,
deadline, /by, /from, /to). These numbers carried no meaning on
their own, and changing a command word or delimiter would silently
break the corresponding offset elsewhere with no compiler warning.

Introduce named constants for each command word and delimiter, and
compute offsets from their .length() instead of restating the
number. This follows the "Avoid Magic Numbers" guideline: a reader
can now see exactly what each offset corresponds to, and the two
values can never drift out of sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract addTask() to remove duplication in TBlade
commitResults.messageBody:
The todo/deadline/event branches of executeCommand() each repeated
the same three steps verbatim: add the task, save the task list,
then build the confirmation message. Each also re-fetched the task
it had just added via tasks.get(tasks.size() - 1) instead of keeping
the reference it already had, an unnecessary indirection that
existed only because the duplicated code didn't have a task
variable in scope to reuse.

Extract a private addTask(Task) helper shared by all three branches.
This removes the triplicated block, keeps a direct reference to the
task instead of re-deriving it by index, and shortens
executeCommand() itself, making the command dispatch easier to scan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Avoid redundant task lookups in mark/unmark handling
commitResults.messageBody:
mark and unmark each called tasks.get(taskIndex) twice: once to
invoke markAsDone()/unmarkAsDone(), and again to pass the task into
the confirmation formatter. The second lookup was pure repetition of
work already done on the previous line.

Cache the task reference once per branch and reuse it for both the
mutation and the formatting call, matching how delete already does
it (via the reference returned by tasks.remove()).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Centralize the default data file path
commitResults.messageBody:
TBlade.main() and gui.Main each hardcoded the literal "data/duke.txt"
independently. The two copies had no enforced relationship, so
changing where TBlade stores its data would require remembering to
update both call sites, and it wasn't obvious from either file alone
that the console and GUI entry points share the same data file.

Add TBlade.DEFAULT_DATA_FILE_PATH as the single source of truth, and
have both entry points reference it instead of restating the string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Main.start() propagate FXML load failures
commitResults.messageBody:
start() caught the IOException from loading MainWindow.fxml and
only printed its stack trace, with no comment explaining why that
was safe. If the load ever actually failed, the method would return
normally without showing a scene or a stage, leaving the user
staring at nothing with no visible error — the empty-looking catch
block was hiding a fatal startup failure instead of handling it.

Application.start() is already declared "throws Exception", so
there's no need to catch IOException here at all: declare
start() as "throws IOException" and let JavaFX's own launch
mechanism report the failure instead.

Verified the GUI still launches normally after this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Fail fast on DialogBox FXML load failure
commitResults.messageBody:
The DialogBox constructor caught the IOException from loading
DialogBox.fxml, printed its stack trace, and then fell straight
through to dialog.setText(text) and displayPicture.setImage(img).
If the load ever actually failed, dialog and displayPicture (both
@FXML-injected by that same load() call) would still be null, so
the very next line would throw an unexplained NullPointerException
instead of a clear one — the catch block wasn't really handling
anything, just delaying and obscuring the real failure.

Rethrow as an unchecked RuntimeException with a message naming the
actual cause. A DialogBox constructor can't declare a checked
exception (it's called from static factories with no throws clause,
in turn called from an @FXML event handler), so unlike Main.start()
this can't simply propagate IOException — wrapping it is the
appropriate fail-fast alternative here.

Verified the GUI still starts and shows its greeting dialog box
normally after this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

find() built its result with a manual accumulate-into-a-list loop:
create an empty ArrayList, then add each task whose description
matched. This is exactly a filter operation, which streams express
more directly.

Replace the loop with tasks.stream().filter(...).collect(...). Use
Collectors.toCollection(ArrayList::new) rather than
Collectors.toList(), since the result must stay mutable — it becomes
the backing list of the returned TaskList wrapper, and Collectors.
toList() makes no mutability guarantee.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for Storage.load() and save()
commitResults.messageBody:
Both methods were manual loop-and-accumulate translations: load()
mapped each stored line to a Task (skipping nulls from corrupted
lines), and save() mapped each Task to its stored line. Both are
plain map (and, for load(), filter) operations.

Replace both loops with streams: load() becomes
readAllLines().stream().map(this::parseTask).filter(Objects::nonNull)
.collect(...), and save() becomes tasks.stream().map(this::formatTask)
.collect(Collectors.toList()). load() keeps
Collectors.toCollection(ArrayList::new) rather than
Collectors.toList(), since the result becomes the backing list of a
TaskList that must support add()/remove() afterward — same reasoning
as TaskList.find()'s earlier stream conversion.

Verified StorageTest's corrupted-line test still skips the bad line
and keeps the valid ones, confirming filter(Objects::nonNull)
behaves exactly like the old null check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix UiTest to use the platform line separator
commitResults.messageBody:
showMessage_printsEachLineWithPigEmoji() hardcoded "\n" as the
expected line separator between printed lines, but Ui.printLine()
uses System.out.println(), which emits the platform line separator
(\r\n on Windows, \n elsewhere). The test passed on Linux/macOS but
failed on Windows, where the actual output had an extra \r the
assertion didn't expect. This was invisible in local development
(everyone on this project develops on macOS/Linux) and only surfaced
once the just-added GitHub Actions CI started running the test suite
on windows-latest too.

The application code was already correct — println() is the right
call here. Fix the test instead: build the expected string with
System.lineSeparator() so it matches actual output on every
platform.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect and reject duplicate tasks on add
commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing stopped the same task from being added multiple times, e.g.
running "todo read book" twice silently created two identical
entries with no way to tell them apart in the list.

Give Task value semantics via equals()/hashCode(), based on type and
description (Deadline and Event extend this with their own date/
time fields, since e.g. two deadlines with the same description but
different due dates are legitimately different tasks). Completion
status is deliberately excluded from equality, so marking a task
done doesn't change what it's considered a duplicate of.

TaskList.add() now checks tasks.contains(task) before adding, and
rejects an exact duplicate with a TBladeException that says what's
wrong and how to fix it. This only guards the add path; tasks
already duplicated in a pre-existing data file are left as-is, since
silently dropping previously-saved data is out of scope for "detect
duplicates on add".

Verified end-to-end: adding the same todo twice is rejected with a
clear message, while a deadline with the same description as an
existing todo is correctly still allowed (different type).

This is the course's "Add an extension" task (category C:
C-DetectDuplicates); the corresponding tag is BCD-Extension per that
task's explicit instruction, not C-DetectDuplicates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
